documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Came in to talk about flying. She has been afraid to fly for about ten years, since around the end of high school, and has not been on a plane at all in that time. She has skipped family gatherings out of state and passed on work trips that would have meant a flight. She knows the numbers, that flying is safer than the drive here, and says it makes no sense to her either. Just picturing being on a plane, her heart races, she sweats and gets a feeling that something terrible is about to happen. Otherwise she feels fine day to day; no worry spilling into the rest of life, sleep okay. What brings her in now: her company has offered her a regional sales rep position, which she really wants, and it means flying regularly.
No meds. NKDA. Mother has anxiety, an uncle on dad's side is afraid of heights.

O: Vitals reviewed. Comfortable, talkative, good eye contact. Heart regular, lungs clear. Mood good, affect full.
PHQ-9 2, GAD-7 4.

A/P: long-standing fear of flying with full avoidance, now costing her a job opportunity. Reads like a specific phobia; rest of the picture is reassuring.
- Referral to psychiatry for evaluation and treatment options; she prefers that to starting with a therapist cold.
- Did not start anything today.
- She'll message if the wait is long.

conditions.label: Specific phobia, situational type (fear of flying)

documents.title: Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — INITIAL EVALUATION
Date of evaluation: 06/24/2024
Referred by: primary care

Reason for referral: fear of flying.

History: Ms. Hossain is a 28-year-old woman who describes roughly a decade of severe fear of air travel. She has avoided flying completely over that period, at the cost of family gatherings she wanted to attend and opportunities at work. She is clear that the fear is out of proportion and that commercial flying carries very little risk; nonetheless the idea of boarding a plane brings on a pounding heart, sweating and a strong sense of dread. She is seeking treatment now because she has been offered a position she very much wants that would involve frequent flying.

Past medical history: none of significance.
Medications: none.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: mother with generalized anxiety disorder; paternal uncle with acrophobia.
Social history: works as a sales support coordinator at a medical device company. Never smoker. Drinks socially, one or two drinks a month.

Examination: general physical examination unremarkable. Mental status: well groomed, cooperative, normal speech, mood 'a little nervous talking about it', affect congruent, thought process linear, no suicidal or homicidal ideation, insight and judgment good.

Impression: Specific phobia, situational type (flying).

Recommendations:
1. Exposure-based cognitive behavioral therapy is the treatment of choice. Provided a list of therapists in the area who do this work.
2. No medication recommended at this time.
3. Follow up here in about six months.

Thank you for the referral.
Allergies: NKDA

documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 12/23/2024

Ms. Hossain returns about six months after her initial evaluation for specific phobia of flying. The main issue now is work. Her current job involves travel that she manages to avoid, and she has turned down a promotion because the new role would have meant getting on planes. Her description of the fear is unchanged: she knows air travel is safe, yet the prospect of a flight still brings racing heart, sweating and a sense of dread. She feels her career is being held back and wants to go over what treatment involves.

She has not yet started therapy; she could not find an in-network therapist with openings.

Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family and social history unchanged from June.

Examination: physical exam unremarkable. Mental status: calm, engaged, mood 'frustrated with myself', affect appropriate, no suicidal ideation, insight good.

Assessment: Specific phobia, situational type (flying), unchanged.

Plan:
- Reviewed what exposure-based CBT looks like in practice, including stepwise exposure and virtual-reality programs used for flying. Remains the recommended treatment. Additional names provided.
- No medication.
- Return as needed or once therapy is under way.

Allergies: NKDA

orders.reason: exposure-based CBT for specific phobia of flying

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — RETURN VISIT
Date of visit: 12/29/2025
Seen by a different psychiatrist in our group than at her prior visits.

Ms. Hossain, 29, comes back for her fear of flying, first assessed here in June 2024 and seen again in December 2024. Things are harder now. Her role at work has changed so that she is expected to fly often, and she is still not getting on planes at all, which is creating real pressure at her job. She describes the same pattern: she knows flying is safe, but even starting to book a ticket sets off palpitations, sweating and a feeling of looming catastrophe. She reports no frightening flight experience of her own and none in her family. She has also been offered a substantial promotion that would require air travel, and she wants to be able to take it.

Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Vital signs: within normal limits.
Examination: no abnormal findings. Mental status: anxious when discussing travel, otherwise euthymic; linear thinking; denies suicidal ideation; good insight.

Assessment: Specific phobia, situational type (flying), with increased impairment from new occupational demands.

Plan:
- Referral placed to a psychologist in our network who provides exposure-based CBT, including virtual-reality exposure for flying. Our staff will help with scheduling so this does not stall again.
- No medication.
- Follow up here as needed.

Allergies: NKDA

documents.title: Psychology Intake Letter
documents.author: psychology
documents.body:
Re: Deepa Hossain, DOB 01/04/1996
Intake date: 02/03/2026

Thank you for the opportunity to see Ms. Hossain, referred by psychiatry for specific phobia of flying. She has avoided air travel entirely for about twelve years and now faces regular flying for work. Her fear centers on being in the cabin with no way off; she has no history of a frightening flight. She is otherwise doing well, on no medications, NKDA.

We agreed on a course of exposure-based cognitive behavioral therapy, weekly to start: education about anxiety and avoidance, a fear hierarchy, and stepwise exposure (imagery and flight videos, virtual-reality flight simulation, then in-person steps at the airport), with the goal of a short flight. She is motivated and understood the plan.

I will update you as treatment progresses.

Allergies: NKDA

documents.title: Psychology Progress Letter
documents.author: psychology
documents.body:
Re: Deepa Hossain, DOB 01/04/1996
Letter dated 05/19/2026

Progress update. Ms. Hossain has attended about 14 sessions of exposure-based CBT since February. She has worked through flight videos and audio, several virtual-reality flight simulations including takeoff and turbulence, and an in-person visit to an airport terminal through check-in. Her distress during exposures has come down steadily and she no longer avoids talking about or planning travel. She has not yet flown. We are moving to sessions every other week while she practices between visits.

No medications. NKDA.

Please contact me with any questions.
